Translate a SAS program into R (tidyverse) code

Source: R/run.R
sas_translate.Rd

The macro processor runs first; steps are translated in order. Nothing is executed, so macro variables created by CALL SYMPUT are not available to later macro code (use sas_run() for that).

Usage

sas_translate(code, work = list(), level = c("auto", "L3"))

Arguments

code

SAS source code.

work

Named list of input data frames available as WORK data sets.

level

"auto" (choose L1/L2/L3 per step) or "L3" (force row loops).

Value

A sasonr_translation object; $steps[[i]]$code holds the R code.

The code of a step calls base R, dplyr::/tibble:: functions and the run-time helpers that sasonr exports (documented as internal). It is evaluated by sas_run() in an environment that holds work (an environment with the WORK data sets as data frames), .log and .lst (character vectors the step appends its log and listing lines to), .meta (the variable attributes the step records), .symtab (the macro symbol table) and .titles (the current TITLE lines), with the session of the run bound for the log NOTEs and _ERROR_. Steps that sasonr runs itself (PROC SQL, PROC DATASETS) have no R translation: their code is a call of sas_untranslated(), which stops with a condition of class sasonr_unsupported.

Option sasonr.passes selects the readability passes applied to the code of vectorised DATA steps: "by_first_value" (a retained numeric variable set only at FIRST. of a BY group from a column becomes one grouped value per BY group) and "unused_first_last" (FIRST./LAST. columns that no later expression reads are not created). All are on by default; options(sasonr.passes = character()) turns them off. A pass rewrites code only where the result is the same: the same WORK data sets and the same log. sas_run() runs the code with the same passes.

Examples

tr <- sas_translate("data b; set a; y = round(x, 0.1); run;",
                    work = list(a = data.frame(x = c(1.25, 2.35))))
tr
#> # ---- DATA B (SAS line 1) -- level L1
#> # L1: no cross-row state
#> .d <- sas_ds(work, "a") |>
#>   sas_note_read("a") |>
#>   dplyr::mutate(y = do.call(sas_f_round, c(sas_mv_args(c(1L, 20L), x, 0.1))))
#> work$b <- .d |> dplyr::select(x, y)
#>
